headline: Probabilistic models of spatial and technical structure in transcriptomic data
label: Probabilistic Inference For Transcriptomics
summary: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomic datasets now demand models that explicitly represent technical noise, spatial dependence, and causal structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit probabilistic modeling of technical and spatial structure in transcriptomic data, most visibly in spatial transcriptomics. GPSNorm jointly models technical and spatial effects through INLA and propagates uncertainty, while RKMR adds spike-and-slab selection with spatial dependence for uncertainty-aware marker panel discovery. Other items apply statistical rigor to different questions: a double machine learning comparison of nuisance-function strategies for causal gene-disease effects in single-cell SLE B cells, a sensitivity-aware benchmark testing when deep representation learning improves scRNA-seq clustering over PCA, and NLCD for nonlinear causal gene relations. Evaluation of Geneformer modifications and Perturb-seq response decomposition extends this concern to single-cell foundation and perturbation models. The new element is treating uncertainty, sensitivity, and causal identification as explicit model components rather than post hoc checks.
